data.narrative:
Theseus is a seed-stage Defense & Security company founded by Stanford and McGill-trained engineers, having raised $4.3M to date. The valuation analysis incorporates a comp universe of 10 peers—2 public and 8 private—spanning seed through Series A stages, including UFORCE, Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, and Saronic.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $4.3M total raised as a base proxy, applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement, yielding $11M. Peer-median analysis across four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables (Stark Defence at $4.0B, UFORCE at $1.0B, Singularity at $400M, NODA AI at $125M) produces a median of $700M, with a range spanning $125M to $4.0B.

The triangulated valuation range is $9M (low) to $805M (high), with a median of $355M. This wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty regarding Theseus's product maturity, commercial traction, and defensibility relative to a heterogeneous peer set. The stage-progression method suggests conservative floor valuation anchored to capital deployed; peer-median valuation reflects the sector's broad valuation distribution but lacks clarity on whether comparables are truly parallel on product development stage and customer acquisition. Key uncertainties include demonstrated technical differentiation, customer pipeline, and path to defensible IP in a crowded Defense & Security landscape.
